fact: Code On The Go (CoGo) is a mobile-first Android IDE for editing, building and deploying Android apps directly on Android phones/tablets.
CoGo is developed by App Dev for All and is the maintained successor to AndroidIDE, which was archived in 2024.
CoGo is offline-capable, but cloud AI, first-run asset downloads, uncached dependencies, Git remotes, updates and plugin catalog access may require connectivity.
CoGo runs real Gradle builds on-device through a tooling API in a separate process and reports build events back to the IDE.
Newer CoGo features follow UI → ViewModel → Repository → data source, using Koin, StateFlow/SharedFlow and UDF; legacy parts still use Android Views, LiveData and EventBus.
CoGo's codebase is mid-migration: new UI is intended to use Jetpack Compose while many existing screens remain View-based.
The architecture describes roughly 80 Gradle modules plus three included composite builds; exact counts can change.
The official materials list Android 9 minimum, ARMv7 and ARM64 support, JDK 21, and bundled Kotlin 1.9.2; verify live compatibility documentation before relying on the snapshot.
The official compatibility discussion estimates about 3.5 GB storage minimum, 1.5 GB free RAM minimum and 4 GB free RAM recommended.
The product page warns that releases 26.38 and later include a breaking core toolchain upgrade for projects created with 26.37 or earlier; follow the migration guide.
CoGo's own Android modules centrally use v7 (armeabi-v7a) and v8 (arm64-v8a) ABI flavors, producing variant-specific task names such as assembleV8Debug.
The inspected architecture branch states CoGo itself uses compile SDK 36, minimum SDK 28 and target SDK 28; these are not universal settings for apps built by users.
CoGo plugins are standalone Android modules packaged as .cgp files, described by the authoring guide as a renamed APK.
The plugin API includes lifecycle hooks initialize, activate, deactivate and dispose, plus context, service registry, metadata, permission and extension interfaces.
Plugin compatibility metadata uses a YY.WW release-week format such as 26.30; min version is enforced in the documented snapshot while max is advisory.
The architecture identifies Gemini via Google's GenAI SDK and on-device llama.cpp as distinct AI integration paths.
The plugin API changelog describes plugin-contributed AI agent tools and an embedding backend capability added in later release weeks.
The architecture identifies JGit as the Git client, and official support materials mention cloning a Git repository from the main menu.
The official product page describes Sketch to UI as a plugin that converts a photographed hand-drawn app layout into Android XML.
The main repository identifies the project as GPL-3.0-or-later; individual dependencies, assets and embedded documentation may have separate licenses.
CoGo's deep-link implementation uses a path traversal/symlink guard for user-controlled file paths rather than naïve path joining.
The architecture states large SDK/bootstrap/Gradle/documentation assets are stored outside the main public repository and fetched or reconstructed during build/release workflows.
Important investigation entry points include README.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, CLAUDE.md, settings.gradle.kts, build logic, app/, plugin-api/, lsp/, editor modules, termux/ and testing/.
The current stage branch is a moving development target and can contain unreleased APIs not present in the latest stable release.

For build failures, first identify whether the failure is Gradle startup/sync, dependency resolution, compilation, packaging, installation or runtime; preserve the first causal error and exact toolchain versions.
